title: Does anyone know a really good AI for generating sound effects?
author: TheKamiBoy
selftext:
I'm making a game with a wide variety of creatures and equipment, and each of them needs very specific sounds. A katana slicing, a robot rebuilding itself, an ice arrow, etc.

Does anyone know an AI that can generate sound effects this specific? The ones I've tried, like ElevenLabs, aren't that good for this kind of thing.

comments.author: GurusCZ
comments.body: Suno has sound creation option but it is not good either

comments.author: Envinsule
comments.body: I haven’t tried it, but I think OpenAI has an audio creation option in their api. Similarly, Gemini can create audio. Have you tried these?

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body: So, in this case, do I just ask Codex to generate an audio file and it generates one? I didn’t know it had that capability, at least not with any real quality.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
Elevenlabs is pretty much top of the stack for this right now unless you want to make them from scratch (which is easier than it sounds). I do this for quite a few things and process them in Audacity. For the harder things I use Elevenlabs.

Prompting is tricky on Elevenlabs, and you have to bump the prompt adherence to 75% or more to really get it to listen to you. Disable the looping effect and adjust the time from AUTO to something more appropriate for what you want (Katana slice \~1 maybe 1.5s)

"A sharp metallic whoosh transitioning into a clean, resonant steel katana blade slicing fast through the air, crisp high-end, studio quality, Foley." - 1.5s 75%

Best of luck. Be well and keep creating.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
There are *massive* sound effect libraries, online, free

[https://freesound.org/](https://freesound.org/)

[https://pixabay.com/sound-effects/](https://pixabay.com/sound-effects/)

Usually, some kind of EQ / filtering / layering / effects on top of these sound effects is what you need.

replies.author: AdStreet4350
replies.body: Yeah like cmon man you don't need to be 100% ia

replies.author: Weaves87
replies.body:
This is where I found a good amount of my sounds. It takes time to sift through but there are some gold nuggets there.

There are also some absolutely excellent sound packs available on itch.io, but again, you gotta dig through a LOT of stuff. And most of the good packs cost money, but paying $5 is nothing if you were ready to prompt for it anyway.

SFX are one of those things that either completely break or dramatically improve immersion, and are imo worth just paying some money for

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: You can probably even ask your AI to sort out your library and match the right sound with the right file, and write a script to handle all of that stuff.

comments.author: Superb-Work6035
comments.body: Suno will do this but you have to prompt VERY specifically.

comments.author: guillermosan
comments.body: Claude Code with access to a sound processing library is giving me great results. I'm using FunDSP. Then you can ask for sounds like you are talking to a synth. Pretty fun.

replies.author: Crinkez
replies.body: What sound processing library do you use?

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: “Actual intelligence” 11 labs does mid shit tbh, just take a day to listen to sounds around you and think about what those sounds could be in a game. I’m having to use my sound engineering for this right now, gonna mix up a skateboard so I can get the right sounds probably also use a chopping board from my kitchen for the pop and kicking sound for tricks and Ollie

comments.author: fkenned1
comments.body: I built an app using claude to generate sfx with Stable Audio 3. I would recommend doing that. It works great.

comments.author: ContactIcy3963
comments.body: Grab free stuff from the internet and pass it to Astra.

comments.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
comments.body: I had a lot better luck with Firefly than I had with ElevenLabs. I was trying to get gun sound effects, so it may depend on what you're trying to generate, but that was my experience.

comments.author: Stock-Requirement779
comments.body:
Depends on the style. For retro blips, jsfxr (sfxr.me) is free and still great, even though it's not AI. ElevenLabs also has a decent general sound effects generator.

Full disclosure, I made one for *exactly* this: https://blipsmith.ai. There are samples on the homepage you can play without signing up, so you can tell if it's any good first. Would love to hear what it gets wrong if you try it.
